extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, licensees, patent agents/attorneys, and patent office officials in India
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on registers, assignments, working of patents, compulsory licensing, government use, and grounds/procedures for revocation under the Indian Patents Act (including Forms, fees, timelines and evidentiary expectations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Register entries required upon grant (S.67)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon grant the Controller shall enter in the register: name, address and nationality of the grantee as patentee; the title of the invention (including categories under section 5); date of the patent; date of grant; and address for service of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller may also enter such other particulars as he thinks fit. The register entry is the formal record of proprietorship and title information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other particulars enterable in register
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries may include notifications of assignment and transmission, licenses under patents, amendments, extensions, revocation, cessation, restoration of lapsed patents, payment of renewal fees, term, surrender, compulsory licences, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller has discretion to enter other particulars; these form part of public record and affect third-party notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particulars regarding proceedings to be entered
rubrics_metrics.description: Controller shall enter particulars regarding proceedings under the Act before the Controller or the courts in respect of every patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures that litigation and administrative actions affecting a patent are reflected in the register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of renewal fee payment
rubrics_metrics.description: On issue of a certificate of payment of the prescribed renewal fee in respect of a patent, the Controller shall enter in the register that the fee has been paid and the date of payment as stated in the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified evidence of payment is recorded to show maintenance of patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alteration of patentee particulars and additional address for service
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may request in writing the alteration of name, nationality, address or address for service; Controller may require proof before acting. At most two addresses for service in India may be entered at any one time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be in writing; Controller exercises discretion and may demand evidence of change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register as evidence — certified copies acceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: The register of patents can be used as evidence in court; duly certified copies of entries serve the purpose — no need to produce the original register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified copies sealed with the Patent Office seal are sufficient proof of register contents in litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments and related documents must be in writing and registered (S.69)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments, transfers, and documents affecting proprietorship are not valid unless in writing and registered. Applications for registration under s.69 must be made (typically using Form 16) with the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation of assignment must be accompanied by two certified true copies; Controller may call for additional proof of title or written consent as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and certification requirements for assignment registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Every assignment or document giving effect to or evidencing transfer must be accompanied by two copies certified to be true copies by the applicant or his agent; Controller may request further proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide the required certified copies or proof may delay or prevent registration of title or interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of title or interest — entry form and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of an application under s.69 the Controller shall register the title or interest and make an entry in the register in prescribed form showing parties, nature of instrument (assignment, mortgage, licence) and dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal register entry records the effect of the instrument on proprietorship; accuracy of the instrument and proof of entitlement are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-ownership entitlement (case guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of an agreement to the contrary, co-owners of equal undivided shares are entitled to equal shares in benefits from assignment of the patent; co-patentees may each initiate references (Florey & Patchett cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law indicates equal sharing by default; existence of contrary agreement must be shown beyond reasonable doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of register by Appellate Board (S.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Appellate Board may, on application by any person aggrieved, rectify the register by making, varying or deleting entries where there is omission, unjust entry, wrong entry remaining, or any error/defect in any entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of applications to the Board shall be given to the Controller who may appear and be heard. Any Board order directs the Controller to rectify the register in the prescribed manner and the rectification shall be served on relevant persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register open for public inspection (S.72)
rubrics_metrics.description: The register shall be open to inspection by the public; certified copies sealed with the Patent Office seal are available on payment of prescribed fee. If records are kept electronically, access to electronic media or printouts shall be provided for inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public access to register entries and certified copies promotes transparency and third-party reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working requirement — patents must be worked in India (S.83)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are granted to encourage inventions and ensure they are worked in India on a commercial scale and to the fullest extent reasonably practicable without undue delay; patentees and licensees must furnish details of working every six months and whenever required by the Controller (S.146).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents should not be mere monopolies for importation; the Controller evaluates working to promote industrial development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation for non-working — procedural requirements (S.85)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for revocation under s.85(1) may be made after expiry of 2 years from date of order granting the first compulsory license; application in Form 19 with prescribed fee; applicant must state nature of interest and terms/conditions of license they will accept (unless Central Government applicant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller assesses whether a prima facie case exists; if not, he notifies and may refuse unless hearing is requested; advertisement and opposition procedures apply (opposition in Form 14 within two months from advertisement). The Controller will set hearing dates with at least 10 days' notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for compulsory licence (S.84)
rubrics_metrics.description: After three years from grant any person interested may apply for compulsory licence on grounds that: (a) reasonable requirements of the public have not been satisfied; (b) the patented invention is not available to the public at a reasonably affordable price; or (c) the patented invention is not worked in India.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A licensee of the patent may also apply. Applications are made in Form 17 with prescribed fees and must state the applicant's interest and facts relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for assessing reasonable price and working in India
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to make patented inventions available at a reasonable price depends on the circumstances of each case. Failure to work within India will be considered with respect to facilities available in India; mere importation when domestic manufacture is possible is a factor. 'Reasonable requirements' includes prejudice to existing trade or its development caused by refusal to grant licenses (see S.84(7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment is case-specific; affordability and availability are fact-sensitive inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations under S.84(6) when deciding grant of compulsory licence
rubrics_metrics.description: Controller takes into account: (i) nature of the invention and time since grant and measures taken by patentee/licensee to make full use of invention (including possible adjournment under s.86(1)); (ii) ability of potential licensee to work the invention and provide capital; (iii) whether applicant made genuine efforts to obtain voluntary licence from patentee (not required in national emergency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors inform whether adequate time/opportunity was given and whether the applicant is capable and sincere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirements and fees for compulsory licence (Form 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application should be made in Form 17 with prescribed fee: Rs.1500 for a natural person and Rs.6000 for others, accompanied by a statement setting out the nature of the applicant’s interest and the facts on which the application is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete factual particulars and evidence supporting grounds are necessary; insufficient applications may be refused at prima facie stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision of terms of compulsory licence (Section 88(4)) — procedure and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An application to revise terms and conditions of a licence settled by the Controller must be in Form 20 with prescribed fee (Rs.1500/6000) and can be made only after 12 months from when the compulsory licensee has started working the invention; application must state facts relied upon and be accompanied by evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prima facie case not made, Controller notifies and may refuse unless hearing requested within one month. If allowed to proceed, the applicant must serve copies on patentee/other interested persons who may oppose within two months. Controller will hear and may amend license terms as deemed necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licence for export of pharmaceutical products (Section 92A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory licence is available for manufacture and export of patented pharmaceutical products to any country having insufficient or no manufacturing capacity in the pharmaceutical sector to address public health problems, provided the importing country has granted/allowed importation or permitted such products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller shall grant a compulsory licence on receipt of prescribed application, solely for manufacture and export, under such terms as specified and published. 'Pharmaceutical products' includes patented product, product made through patented process, necessary ingredients and diagnostic kits. The provision is to be used in good faith to address public health, interpreted liberally (including when importing country has no patent). Application in Form 17 with fees applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government use of inventions — scope and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Government or any person authorized by it may use a patented invention anytime after filing or grant for Government purposes. Use before the priority date by Government entails no royalty/remuneration. Use after grant should be on agreed terms or, failing agreement, decided by the High Court under s.103. Government may authorize third parties to use the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where Government authorizes use, Central Government should inform patentee of extent of use unless contrary to public interest. Rights include selling goods produced and purchasers may deal with goods as if Government were the patentee. Agreements that restrict Government use or require payment for Government use have no effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition by Central Government and compensation/dispute resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Central Government may acquire an invention for public purpose by publishing a notification in the Official Gazette. Notice of acquisition must be given to the applicant/patentee and persons in the register who have interest. Compensation should be given as agreed or, in default, determined by the High Court under s.103. Disputes regarding Government use may be referred to the High Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Government deems disclosure prejudicial to public interest it may confidentially disclose documents to the advocate of the other party in High Court proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for grant of compulsory licence (overview and timelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application under Patents Rules (Rule 96 as amended) is filed on Form 17 with prescribed fees. If Controller is satisfied prima facie case under s.87 is made, he directs serving copies on patentee and publishes the application; patentee may oppose. Controller shall order grant upon such terms as he deems fit (see s.90). Normal time for grant may not exceed six months. In national emergency/public non-commercial use the procedure under s.87 may not apply and licences may be granted immediately under s.92(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific regimes (Section 92, 92A, export cases) have tailored procedures; Controller secures that articles manufactured under licence shall be available to public at lowest prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate/expedited compulsory licence in emergencies and anti-competitive contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: In national emergency, extreme urgency or public non-commercial use (including public health crises like AIDS, HIV, TB, malaria), compulsory licences may be granted immediately under s.92(3). For semiconductor technology or licences to remedy anti-competitive practices, the license may be limited to public non-commercial use or permit export as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedited grants bypass normal procedural delays to address urgent public needs; terms aim to ensure availability at low prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of patents — standing and fora (CH XI)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be revoked by the High Court at any time during its life on petition by any person interested, by the Central Government (via the Appellate Board), or on a counterclaim by a defendant in an infringement suit (subject to Act provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation can be sought through various procedural routes; counterclaims in infringement suits are a common vehicle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for revocation: invention claimed is subject of prior grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent may be revoked if a claim in the patent to be revoked is identical to a claim in a patent of earlier priority date and the earlier claim is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority date/earlier valid claims are determinative; overlapping identical claims can be invalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for revocation: patentee not entitled to the patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Revocation may follow if the patent was obtained by a person not among those categories entitled to apply under s.6 (the 'true and first inventor' concept excludes, e.g., first importer or person to whom invention was first communicated from outside India).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only persons entitled under the Act may obtain patents; improper applicants can have patents revoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for revocation: patent wrongfully obtained by person other than entitled
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent has been wrongfully obtained by any person, the person entitled to apply may petition for revocation — petitioner must be a person entitled to apply for the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ground addresses wrongful procurement by a non-entitled person; factual proof of entitlement is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for revocation: subject of a claim is not an invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be revoked where the subject-matter of a claim does not satisfy the statutory definition of 'invention' under s.2(1)(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the claimed subject-matter falls within the statutory invention definition and excludes non-inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for revocation: lack of novelty (anticipation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent can be revoked if the invention lacks novelty with regard to prior knowledge or prior use; novelty is an essential prerequisite for patentability (examiners search prior publications and patents under s.13 and Controller can refuse under s.15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public knowledge can be oral or documented; mere publication is not automatically sufficient — the publication must have been such that the concerned person was free to share the information. Internet publications are considered in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for revocation: obviousness / lack of inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents may be revoked where claimed subject-matter is obvious or lacks an inventive step compared to prior knowledge or prior use. 'Obvious' means easily perceived or plainly evident to a person of fair knowledge in the field; inventive step is the converse of obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court examines how the invention was arrived at and whether a skilled person could have developed it without substantial inventive step; state-of-the-art and public knowledge are reference points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for revocation: invention not useful (lack of utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent may be revoked if invention is not useful — i.e., it will not work or will not provide the desired result in the specification. Practical or commercial utility is not required; utility judged against state of the art at patent date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrable operability is required; if invention does not perform as claimed, utility ground may succeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for revocation: insufficient description (lack of sufficiency/enablement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention is not sufficiently described in the specification — the complete specification must describe an embodiment of each claim so as to enable those skilled in the art to practise the invention 'without making further invention' — the patent can be revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description must be fair, sufficiently detailed and not unnecessarily difficult to follow; sufficiency is judged on the merits of the specification (case law cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for revocation: claim not clearly defined and/or not fairly based
rubrics_metrics.description: Two independent grounds: (i) the scope of any claim is not sufficiently and clearly defined; (ii) the claim is not fairly based on matter disclosed in the specification (see s.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fairly based means the monopoly sought should be no broader than justified by disclosed matter; patentee should not claim more than the disclosure warrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for revocation: obtained by false suggestion or representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent may be revoked if it was obtained by false suggestion or representation in relation to the specification or any fact/statement required to be made in connection with grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No limitation on nature of falsehood — material misrepresentations can vitiate grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for revocation: subject of claims not a patentable invention (sections 3 & 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent can be revoked where the claims relate to matter excluded from patentability under sections 3 and 4 (e.g., certain methods, substances, or other statutory exclusions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate claim subject-matter against statutory exclusions; some categories may be non-applicable depending on claim type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for revocation: prior secret use before priority date
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be revoked if the claimed invention was secretly used before the priority date, except as limited by section 64(3) and relevant case law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secret prior use that deprives novelty may invalidate the patent; factual proof of such secret use is required.
